decisionStandardAnswers.2_data_sparsity_major_cause: PARTIAL — real but small-n effect (see sparsity-analysis.json: 0-1 games-played bucket n=76, gap +2.97 MAE vs +0.6-0.7 elsewhere; fallback-tier-downgraded n=108, gap +2.73 vs +0.73)
decisionStandardAnswers.3_errors_persistent_by_team: WEAK — lag-1 residual correlation 0.061 (near-zero); market-vs-model DISAGREEMENT persistence is much stronger (lag-1 correlation 0.36)
decisionStandardAnswers.4_overreact_or_underreact: NEITHER — rating volatility has ~zero correlation with next-week model error (-0.02) or with model-market disagreement (0.09); no evidence of Ridge overreaction
decisionStandardAnswers.5_preseason_prior_staleness_important: YES, moderately — stale-prior team-sides (top/bottom decile of prior-vs-current gap) show +1.03 to +1.25 MAE gap vs +0.68 for stable teams
decisionStandardAnswers.6_qb_continuity_feasible_and_valuable: FEASIBLE (GO); VALUE small but real (largest in extreme-disagreement subset: +0.0013 R2 over IPR alone)
decisionStandardAnswers.7_transfer_feasible_and_valuable: FEASIBLE for 2021+ only (GO); VALUE negligible (~0.00004 R2 gain over IPR alone)
decisionStandardAnswers.8_coaching_continuity_feasible: FEASIBLE (GO); VALUE small (largest single-feature gain over IPR alone: +0.0045 R2)
decisionStandardAnswers.9_context_variables_useful: MIXED — rematch and bye-week context show real gap reduction; short-rest sample too small (n=149) to be conclusive; travel distance NOT AVAILABLE
decisionStandardAnswers.10_most_likely_to_close_gap: Schedule-network connectivity / cross-conference sparsity (component-count 10+ bucket: +1.92 MAE gap vs +0.63 fully connected) and nonconference-game context (+1.40 vs +0.62) show the LARGEST effect sizes of anything tested — larger than any single roster/coaching/QB feature

rankedInformationGapRoadmap.effectSizeSummary: MAE gap +1.92 (high fragmentation, n=254) vs +0.63 (fully connected, n=3326); early season (wk1-3) +1.62 vs +0.66 (wk4+)
rankedInformationGapRoadmap.recommendation: Highest-priority follow-up. Not implemented as a feature in Phase 7 (diagnostic only per Section 14/15) — a future phase could test faster cross-cluster propagation (e.g. a connectivity-aware regularization schedule) without adding new data.
Worth a dedicated follow-up phase testing faster within-season decay for teams flagged as stale (no new data required — reuses existing prior/current rating fields).

rankedInformationGapRoadmap.item: Data sparsity (games played, fallback prior tier)
rankedInformationGapRoadmap.effectSizeSummary: MAE gap +2.97 (0-1 games, n=76) and +2.73 (fallback-tier-downgraded, n=108) vs ~+0.7 baseline — large effect but very small, early-season-only sample
rankedInformationGapRoadmap.recommendation: Confirms the known early-season weakness; not a new data project, just a reminder that Phase 3's fallback tiers ARE where the gap concentrates most.

rankedInformationGapRoadmap.effectSizeSummary: R2 gain +0.0045 over IPR alone (largest of the three implemented candidate blocks), but only +0.00035 over market+model
rankedInformationGapRoadmap.recommendation: Cheap to keep (data already fetched); small IPR-only value. Worth carrying into a future ratings-blend experiment, not urgent on its own.

rankedInformationGapRoadmap.effectSizeSummary: R2 gain +0.0006 over IPR alone (all weeks), +0.0013 in the extreme-disagreement subset — largest where it matters most, but still small in absolute terms
rankedInformationGapRoadmap.recommendation: Feasible and directionally useful, concentrated exactly where the spec hypothesized (extreme disagreements). Worth a deeper follow-up (e.g. weighting by pass-attempt-share magnitude, not just a binary flag) before concluding it's not valuable.

rankedInformationGapRoadmap.recommendation: Not worth pursuing further as a simple net-count feature. A usage-weighted or incoming-starter-only version might behave differently but was out of scope here (Section 9 prohibits a subjective transfer-rating model).

rankedInformationGapRoadmap.recommendation: Documented as a likely market information advantage that cannot yet be tested (Section 8). Would require a dedicated, carefully-sourced ingestion project; explicitly out of scope for this phase.

notWorthPursuing: Transfer portal net-count as a simple feature (near-zero incremental value)
worthPursuing: Schedule-network connectivity / faster cross-cluster opponent adjustment
Faster preseason-prior decay for stale-prior teams
QB continuity as a magnitude-weighted (not binary) feature
Coaching continuity retained as a small, cheap IPR input for a future ratings-blend experiment
overallInterpretation: None of the three implemented candidate blocks (QB continuity, transfer net movement, coaching continuity) meaningfully close the ~0.42 vs ~0.0003 incremental-R2 gap from Phase 6. The two largest effect sizes found in Phase 7 are STRUCTURAL, not roster-information gaps: schedule-network fragmentation/cross-conference sparsity and preseason-prior staleness. This suggests the market's advantage over IPR is currently driven less by information IPR is missing about players/coaches and more by how IPR resolves rating uncertainty across a sparsely-connected schedule graph and how slowly its preseason prior decays for fast-moving teams.
